verdicts.title: Chern--Simons Terms as an Example of the Relations Between Mathematics and Physics
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The inevitability of Chern--Simons terms in constructing a variety of physical models, and the mathematical advances they in turn generate, illustrates the unexpected but profound interactions between the two disciplines.

verdicts.title: Strong Linear Correlation Between Eigenvalues and Diagonal Matrix Elements
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We investigate eigenvalues of many-body systems interacting by two-body forces as well as those of random matrices. We find a strong linear correlation between eigenvalues and diagonal matrix elements if both of them are sorted from the smaller values to larger ones. By using this linear correlation we are able to predict reasonably all eigenvalues of given shell model Hamiltonian without complicated iterations.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns linear correlations between eigenvalues and diagonal matrix elements in many-body physics and random matrices, with no mention of Frobenius-Schur indicators, Boolean satisfiability, or Frege proof depth. It shares only the generic concept of 'linear correlation' and does not interact with the specific cross-field claim.

verdicts.title: The Linear Correlation of $P$ and $NP$
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: $P \overset{\text{?}}{=} NP$ or $P\ vs\ NP$ is the core problem in computational complexity theory. In this paper, we proposed a definition of linear correlation of derived matrix and system, and discussed the linear correlation of $P$ and $NP$. We draw a conclusion that $P$ is linearly dependent and there exists $NP$ which is is linearly independent and take a 3SAT instance which belongs to $NP$ as the example , that is, $P \neq NP$.
